Mia believes that trying new things keeps life fresh. The school lab looked quieter than usual that evening. Mia is saving money to buy a ticket to Toronto. What's more, mom baked a fresh batch of cookies for the school fair.

Jack always says that small steps matter more than big plans. The science corner has become an important part of daily life. Mia wrote down every idea in a small notebook. Also, steel bollards keep delivery vans off the pedestrian street.

Mia will take part in a chess match in March. People around Mia often share different ideas about the school lab. Sometimes a short talk can solve a big problem. What's more, the town needs more employment for young people.

What matters most is not speed, but keeping on. Jack and Mia are preparing a report about the school lab. At first, Mia found it difficult to keep the habit. Also, careful records help the stud farm avoid inbreeding among its horses.
Little by little, things began to change. There is still a long way to go, but the direction is right. On Wednesday evenings, Mia reviews the notes from class.
